title: decade draws its UI as GPU elements, not a cell raster
body:
decade draws all of its own UI through a grid of monospace cells. `Grid` in `src/grid.rs` holds a char, colours and a `right_half` flag per cell. `chrome::raster` and `text::rasterize` fill an RGBA buffer cell by cell on the CPU and cut every glyph to its cell. `render` in `src/compositor.rs` uploads full-window textures built from grids: the chrome, which `patch_chrome` patches cell by cell, then the bars layer, the palette overlay and the drag ghost. The two-cell icons and the private-use edge glyphs from `edge_char` work around the cell limit.

The grid shows in the palette. Text and icons get cut at their cell, sizes and padding move in whole cells, and corners are box-drawing characters. Jack decided on 2026-11-07 that decade should not have a cell renderer. Looking like a TUI is a design constraint: monospace text, thin straight lines, flat fills, and pane chrome aligned to cells. decade breaks that constraint where it helps, for example with pixel padding, rounded corners or a larger font in floating UI.

## Proposal

`render` builds decade's UI as GPU render elements each frame, next to the client surfaces it already draws. Pane layout stays in cells (`CellRect`), because the clients are terminals.

- Fills and 1 px lines are `SolidColorRenderElement`.
- Rounded rects with an optional border come from a small custom pixel shader through smithay's `PixelShaderElement`.
- Each text run is rasterized with swash into a texture sized to the run, cached by text, size and colour, and drawn as a `TextureRenderElement` at a pixel position.
- `Grid`, `chrome::raster`, `patch_chrome`, `edge_char`, `right_half`, and the full-window bars, overlay and ghost textures are removed.

## Open

- How many elements a frame holds once every pane's chrome is elements, and whether `draw_render_elements` stays fast at that count. Nobody has measured it.
